100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 3, 1926, the world watched as the British Empire celebrated the end of its general strike, which had paralyzed industry for nearly nine days, causing widespread unrest. In Germany, Chancellor Hans Luther faced mounting pressure as economic instability continued to challenge the Weimar Republic. Meanwhile, in the United States, tensions rose over the ongoing Prohibition, with calls for its repeal growing among various factions.
